articles.title: Is Neko Health’s body scan worth it? Spotify billionaire’s startup has come to America
articles.full_text:
Spotify founder Daniel Ek’s Neko Health raised $700 million to build a business around scanning your body, but it’s not the only company centering its roadmap around a new kind of preventative healthcare. Midjourney is building its own body scanner, while Function Health has also raised significant capital to build out its preventative-health platform. Why are investors betting so big on this category? 

On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Dominic-Madori Davis talks with Farooq Abbasi, founder and general partner of Preface Ventures and an investor in Neko Health, about how Neko compares with other consumer-health startups. They discuss what has to happen for body scanning to become part of the broader healthcare system.

articles.summary:
Investors are pouring hundreds of millions into startups that want to reinvent preventative healthcare through full-body scanning technology. A recent TechCrunch Equity podcast episode explored why this category is attracting such massive capital.

  • Core event: Spotify founder Daniel Ek's Neko Health raised $700 million to build a business around body scanning, signaling strong investor confidence in preventative-health startups.
  • Broader trend: Neko is not alone — Midjourney is developing its own body scanner, and Function Health has also raised significant funding to expand its preventative-health platform.
  • Expert insight: On the Equity podcast, host Dominic-Madori Davis spoke with Farooq Abbasi, founder of Preface Ventures and a Neko Health investor, about how Neko stacks up against other consumer-health startups.
  • Key question: The discussion centered on what needs to happen for body scanning to be integrated into the broader healthcare system rather than remaining a niche consumer offering.
